names_note: **Word Gets Round**, the room's pick (all three, rework round 4 vote), kept under Robin's note: it names the person's gift (they pass on what they know), not the glass, so the Jack Rose leaves it true. Also on record: *In the Know* (leans on *Where You Stand*'s tagline), *Odd Sizes* (about the case more than the person), *Worth Asking* (*Worth the Trip* already starts with "Worth").
open_items: **For Robin (Wren, carried from the first pour): whoYouAre's "So I'll name it."** is kept verbatim under Robin's note (variety rule V2); it's flagged for him, not rewritten.

**For Robin (a note, not a flag): how far does D12 reach?** Tomás (the drink's owner) ruled the room's v1, a vodka Collins built the *Codex* way, the same cocktail as *Not Too Polite*'s Tom Collins (caregiver-outlaw), so it went; Hester agreed (Oxford files the Vodka Collins inside TOM COLLINS, pdf 2042, the same formula with the spirit swapped). Wren's view was no (the spirit changes kind) and she asks whether D12 reaches any spirit swap in an unchanged template, or only a same-kind one.

**The drink went from a bourbon Rickey (first pour) to a vodka Collins (rework v1, dropped) to a Jack Rose (rework v2):** apple brandy after the *Codex* (p. 129), not Oxford's applejack (pdf 1090); short and shaken, against Wren's earlier long lean, because every long lime drink is now a sibling's or a near twin. 19.3% / 8.22 g / 0.830%, every reading in range; 5 ml of lime either way goes OUT.

**Jack Rose fences (Hester's card C1–C6):** never "the classic is made with apple brandy"; the name is "apparently" the Jacqueminot rose; the gambler "Bald Jack" Rose and the 1912 murder case stay out; no inventor is proven; the grenadine-as-know-how strand is a collection motif (*The Long Answer*, *By Design*), so it stays in the recipe only.

**Story fences (Heugel card):** size isn't quality (no page says odd-sized limes are as good); the key-lime yield conflict stays out; Heugel's present status is not on any page read. Wren's story test point 5 (no promotion story) fails to the letter and stays waived, as in the first pour.
